references.context: Commutative algebra: polynomial algebra R[X_i : i in I] over a commutative unital coefficient ring R, for an arbitrary set I of independent indeterminates; each polynomial has finite monomial support. Includes the one-variable and finite-variable cases and polynomial algebras over fields and quotient coefficient rings.
references.matching_note: Reviewed original source's polynomial expression with the common multivariate-polynomial construction. Index-set size and base coefficient ring specialize the same general commutative unital polynomial algebra; do not conflate it with localization, polynomial evaluation, the polynomial quotient or degree.

references.context: Commutative algebra: quotient of the commutative polynomial ring R[x_1,…,x_n] by the ideal generated by finitely many polynomial relations f_1,…,f_c; the quotient consists of cosets with induced ring operations and its R-algebra structure.
references.reason: Quotient-ring formation is a reusable operation and should not be confused with the polynomial ring, finite-presentation property, or zero locus of relations.
references.matching_note: Compare generic quotient-ring candidate missing.50fc57153b93520a247a and finite-presentation instance missing.2fe33a0bd27720bf99b2; do not alias automatically.

references.context: Commutative algebra: base-change κ(p)-algebra S⊗_R κ(p) of a unital commutative R-algebra S, with multiplication (s⊗a)(t⊗b)=st⊗ab, unit 1⊗1 and κ(p)-algebra structure.

references.context: Elementary number theory: positive integer p>1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and p; equivalently a prime integer, distinct from a prime ideal and from a prime-power integer.
references.reason: Primality of an integer is an independently reusable number-theoretic condition, not supplied by the existing cardinality or positive-natural-number notions.
references.matching_note: Compare exact existing candidate missing.16d2c0615065e12050a2, preserving the distinction between prime integers p and prime ideals of rings.

references.disposition: Prime-power size is a theorem about finite fields, not an additional defining condition or a source of arbitrary finite cardinalities.

references.phrase: inverse system of R-modules indexed by a preorder

references.context: Module/category theory: for R-linear transition u_ij:M_i→M_j in a direct system and R-module N, the reverse Hom transition u_ij^*:Hom_R(M_j,N)→Hom_R(M_i,N), f↦f∘u_ij, by precomposition; these assemble an inverse system.
references.reason: Contravariant precomposition on Hom groups is a reusable functorial map, not captured by the existence of Hom modules alone.
references.matching_note: Compare precomposition candidate missing.37b0713211a5069fde53 and Hom-complex constructions; distinguish covariance from the inverse direction of the transition.

references.phrase: eventual image stabilization at every stage
references.disposition: This is precisely the Mittag-Leffler inverse-image condition, not stabilization of the M_i themselves.

references.phrase: arbitrary direct product ∏_j Q_j of R-modules
references.context: Module theory: product of an arbitrary indexed family of R-modules (Q_j)_{j∈J}, consisting of all tuples (q_j)∈∏_jQ_j with coordinatewise addition and scalar action; unlike a direct sum, supports need not be finite.
references.reason: The product of modules is a reusable categorical/module construction and is distinct from direct sums and tensor products.
references.matching_note: Compare existing product candidate missing.1ebcea580e20705b243c for countable systems but retain arbitrary index sets and empty-product convention.

references.context: Module theory: canonical R-linear tensor/product comparison induced by product projections π_j:∏_iQ_i→Q_j, mapping m⊗(q_i)_i to (m⊗q_j)_j; its injectivity for every family is the Mittag-Leffler criterion.
references.reason: The canonical comparison map arises functorially from tensor and product projections and is meaningful independently from whether it is injective; the injectivity quantifier defines the given Mittag-Leffler property.
references.matching_note: Do not recursively link this to an equivalent Mittag-Leffler criterion as its own prerequisite; preserve arbitrary-family quantifier and distinguish pure-projective conditions.

references.context: Set theory: injectivity of an arbitrary map f:X→Y, meaning f(x)=f(y) implies x=y for all x,y in X; for structured maps this is the underlying-set condition.
references.matching_note: Source occurrence 'injectivity of the canonical tensor/product comparison' expresses ordinary injectivity of the underlying map; distinguish universal injectivity/pure module maps and categorical coproduct structure arrows.

references.disposition: The formulation cites an equivalent criterion; no unlisted equivalence is silently treated as a new definition.
